title: Mobile onboarding
prompt: Design the second step of a three-step onboarding flow for "Sprout", a mobile app that helps people keep houseplants alive with watering reminders. iPhone, 390x844, one screen. This step asks the user which plants they own. Include: an iOS status bar, a progress indicator showing step 2 of 3, a back control, a short headline and one-line helper text, a searchable selection of plants shown as a 2-column grid of 6 selectable tiles (Monstera, Snake plant, Pothos, Fiddle-leaf fig, ZZ plant, Peace lily) each with an image and name, with Monstera and Pothos already selected, a "2 selected" summary, and a fixed bottom primary button "Continue" plus a secondary "Skip for now" text action. Friendly but not childish.
requiredContent: 2-column grid of 6 plant tiles with image and name: Monstera, Snake plant, Pothos, Fiddle-leaf fig, ZZ plant, Peace lily
Primary button Continue and secondary Skip for now
constraints: Respect safe areas (status bar top, home indicator bottom)

checklist.text: A status bar is present at the top and no content collides with it.
Progress clearly communicates step 2 of 3 (dots, segments or text).
Exactly six plant tiles appear in a 2-column grid with the six specified names.
Every tile has a real plant image or illustration (no gray boxes or empty placeholders).
Monstera and Pothos are visibly selected (check, ring or fill) and the other four are visibly not selected.
A "2 selected" summary is visible and consistent with the selection state.
"Continue" is the most prominent control, full-width or nearly so, anchored near the bottom above the home indicator area.
Side margins are consistent (about 16-24px) and tiles align to the same left and right edges.
Tap targets (back, tiles, buttons) look at least ~44px tall.
Body/helper text is at least 13px and readable against its background.
No text is clipped, truncated mid-word unintentionally, or overlapping.
A search field is present above the grid.
The screen fits 390x844; nothing important is cut off at the bottom.
